charts.summary: Query result contains a single region (Germany) with a net profit margin of ~33.68% (0.3368414574). Germany’s total net profit is $8,209,500, total revenue $24,372,000, total operating expense $16,162,500, average operating expense per branch $808,125, and 5 branches. The chart is a scatter plot of Net Profit Margin (y) vs Avg Operating Expense (x) with point size representing total net profit and color by region; tooltips show the numeric details.

chart_spec.title: Net Profit Margin vs Avg Operating Expense by Region

charts.sql:
SELECT
  region,
  SUM(net_profit_usd) AS total_net_profit_usd,
  SUM(revenue_usd) AS total_revenue_usd,
  CASE WHEN SUM(revenue_usd) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE SUM(net_profit_usd) / NULLIF(SUM(revenue_usd),0) END AS net_profit_margin,
  SUM(operating_expense_usd) AS total_operating_expense_usd,
  AVG(operating_expense_usd) AS avg_operating_expense_usd,
  COUNT(DISTINCT branch_name) AS branch_count
FROM public.branch_finance_kpis
WHERE region IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY region
ORDER BY net_profit_margin DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 200;

charts.summary: From Jan to Apr 2025 the average loan default rate steadily decreased from 2.21% to 2.008% while approved loans rose from 1,431 to 1,533 and total net profit increased—suggesting improving portfolio performance as volume grew. The chart shows monthly approved loans as bars (left axis) with the average default rate as a line (right axis) so you can track volume vs credit quality.

chart_spec.title: Monthly Approved Loans and Avg Loan Default Rate (%)

charts.sql:
SELECT
  report_month,
  ROUND(AVG(loan_default_rate_pct)::numeric, 4) AS avg_loan_default_rate_pct,
  SUM(approved_loans_count) AS total_approved_loans_count,
  SUM(net_profit_usd) AS total_net_profit_usd
FROM public.branch_finance_kpis
GROUP BY report_month
ORDER BY report_month
LIMIT 200;

charts.summary: This chart shows daily intraday volatility (Daily High–Low as a percent of Open) over time for each stock index (line, colored by index) with trading volume displayed as semi-transparent bars on a separate (independent) Y axis. Tooltips expose date, index, volatility (%), trading volume and raw high-low range so you can inspect individual days.

chart_spec.title: Daily Volatility (%) vs Trading Volume by Date and Index

charts.sql:
SELECT
  NULLIF(trim("Date"), '')::date AS date,
  "Stock Index" AS stock_index,
  ("Daily High" - "Daily Low") AS high_low_range,
  CASE WHEN "Open Price" IS NULL OR "Open Price" = 0 THEN NULL ELSE (("Daily High" - "Daily Low") / "Open Price") * 100 END AS volatility_pct,
  "Trading Volume" AS trading_volume
FROM public.finance_economics_dataset
WHERE "Daily High" IS NOT NULL AND "Daily Low" IS NOT NULL AND "Trading Volume" IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY date ASC
LIMIT 200;

charts.summary: Line chart showing month-over-month trends (Jan–Apr 2025) of customer accounts and deposits (USD) for each branch. All branches show steady increases in both accounts and deposits; Frankfurt Main has the highest levels (≈13,460 accounts and $22,350,000 deposits in Apr 2025). The first month for each branch has null MoM percent values because there is no prior month to compare.

chart_spec.title: Customer Accounts and Deposits (USD) Trends by Branch (Jan–Apr 2025)

charts.sql:
WITH t AS (
  SELECT branch_name,
         report_month,
         customer_accounts,
         deposits_usd,
         LAG(customer_accounts) OVER (PARTITION BY branch_name ORDER BY report_month) AS prev_customer_accounts,
         LAG(deposits_usd) OVER (PARTITION BY branch_name ORDER BY report_month) AS prev_deposits_usd
  FROM public.branch_finance_kpis
  WHERE report_month IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT branch_name,
       report_month,
       customer_accounts,
       deposits_usd,
       ROUND((customer_accounts::numeric - prev_customer_accounts::numeric) / NULLIF(prev_customer_accounts::numeric,0) * 100, 2) AS customer_accounts_mom_pct,
       ROUND((deposits_usd - prev_deposits_usd) / NULLIF(prev_deposits_usd,0) * 100, 2) AS deposits_usd_mom_pct
FROM t
ORDER BY branch_name, report_month
LIMIT 200;
